chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa' from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out from the Masjid and his riding animal had been lost. So he said: 'If Allah returns it to me, I will thank Allah with the true thanksgiving.' He said: 'So it was not long before it was brought to him, so he said: 'The praise is for Allah.' A man said to him: 'May I be your ransom, did you not say: I will thank Allah with the true thanksgiving?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Did you not hear me say: The praise is for Allah?'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a phrase of respect)

ai.seo_question: What is the true meaning of thanking Allah (shukr) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refines the understanding of *shukr* by demonstrating that the immediate utterance of 'Al-hamdu lillah' upon receiving a favor fulfills the obligation of gratitude, even if the initial vow was more emphatic. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the sufficiency of verbal acknowledgment as an act of worship, distinguishing between the emotional intensity of the vow and the ritual completion of praise. It serves as a practical guide for believers to recognize that gratitude is not merely a future intention but an immediate recognition of divine providence.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> went out from the Masjid and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> had lost his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> (riding) animal. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘If Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> were to Return it to me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> will thank Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> as it is a right of thanking Him<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So, it wasn’t long before they came with it. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’. So a sayer said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! Did you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> not say, ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> will thank Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> as it is a right of thanking Him<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’?’ So Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Did you not listen to me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> saying: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’?’
en.sarwar: 18. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) came out of the Mosque and his animal that he had ridden was missing. The Imam said, ‘If Allah will return my animal I will thank Him the way He must be thanked.’ Not long thereafter his animal was brought back. The Imam said, ‘All praise belongs to Allah.’ Someone then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, did you not say, “I will thank Allah the way He must be thanked?’” The Imam said, ‘Did you not hear me saying, “All praise belongs to Allah?’””
